headline: High: open-webui’s broad networked, persistent, tool-using defaults can amplify unsafe outputs from the non-runnable docs-only companion into leakage, conflicts, and cascading actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a docs-only, non-runnable list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot inject directly. Profile B ingests files, MCP, OpenAPI tools, and browser content by default, and its tool-use pattern is permissive enough that attacker-controlled content from A-like sources could be treated as instructions if bridged in. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b prompts, files, or MCP inputs
IF agent_b parses external content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of external text into agent_b prompts
Add a manual review step before agent_b executes tool calls from imported content
Restrict agent_b MCP/OpenAPI connectors to allowlisted endpoints
Use a provenance tag on imported documents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-separation guards

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. Agent B touches files, documents, notes, persistent memory, and API keys, and it has broad network egress plus file and cloud connectors. If the pair shares a workspace or imported files, B can transmit sensitive material outward; the pairwise risk is therefore medium rather than low because B’s default surfaces are networked.
conditions: IF agent_b is connected to any workspace containing secrets, API keys, or private documents
IF agent_b is allowed to send file contents to external APIs or search services
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace before starting agent_b
Disable external API/search connectors in agent_b for sensitive sessions
Mount only a read-only, redacted data volume into agent_b
Rotate any API keys exposed to agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce per-connector data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable state. Agent B supports files, mounted volumes, subprocesses, and persistent shared sessions, which can conflict with other instances or external writers if they share the same workspace. Because A is effectively read-only, the conflict is one-sided but still exists around shared mutable resources used by B.
conditions: IF agent_b shares a mounted volume or session store with another writer
IF agent_b modifies files or session state while another process also writes them
mitigations: Assign agent_b a dedicated workspace directory
Avoid concurrent writes to the same mounted volume
Pause other writers during agent_b runs
Use file-level backups before edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared session and file state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A provides curated content but no runnable behavior, while agent B can browse, call tools, and act on persistent sessions. If B treats imported A-derived content as authoritative, errors can cascade into tool actions or published outputs. The pair is not high because A does not itself generate executable actions, but B’s default tool use makes the chain plausible.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-derived content as a source of truth without verification
IF agent_b takes actions based on unreviewed summaries or citations
mitigations: Require human review before agent_b acts on imported content
Cross-check A-derived claims against primary sources
Disable auto-execution of tool outputs in agent_b
Log provenance for imported facts
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A is an open-source docs-only resource with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency issue. Agent B handles documents, files, analytics, and API keys, and its connectors can move data to third-party services and cloud storage. If regulated data is placed into B, compliance gaps can arise from retention or residency mismatches; A is not the compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated personal data, secrets, or customer documents are loaded into agent_b
IF agent_b connectors route that data to external services without a DPA or residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b sessions
Disable cloud connectors for regulated workloads
Review retention settings before upload
Limit agent_b to local-only inference for sensitive data
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
